whatis.intro: A unit price is the cost of one unit of a product: the pack price divided by how many units the pack holds. The unit can be an item, a pound or an ounce. Two packs only compare fairly when both are priced on the same unit.

cards.title: Price per quantity, blind to grade
cards.body: Price against quantity, and nothing about quality. Option A's $1.00 a pound only beats Option B's $1.11 if the product inside is the same grade.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the price and quantity a unit price counts

cards.title: Net weight is not always usable weight
cards.body: A can's net weight includes the liquid it is packed in. When the account uses only the solids, compare on drained weight instead.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for drained weight against net weight

cards.title: Catch weight cases price by the pound
cards.body: Meat and cheese often ship catch weight, so every case weighs a little differently. There the price per pound is the real price, and the case price moves each time.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for catch weight cases priced by the pound

who.intro: Pack choice falls to a distributor's buyers and pricing staff, who run it whenever two sizes of one product compete. Anyone comparing them should put both on one base before either is quoted.

look.h2: Put both unit prices on the same footing
look.intro: The division is simple. The weights and counts you type in are where most comparisons slip, and these three checks catch it.

steps.title: Weights in the same measure
steps.body: Pounds against pounds. A spec sheet in ounces or grams has to be converted before it goes in, or the per pound line comes out badly wrong.

steps.title: A count that matches the price
steps.body: A case may be listed by the sleeve or the inner pack, and a price sheet may quote either one. Count the units the price actually covers.

steps.title: Prices from the same date
steps.body: Take both prices from the same week. A pack quoted last month against one quoted today mixes a price change into a size comparison.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits once you pick a pack
vos.h3: Customers check each line before it reaches you
vos.body: VOS does not compare packs or buy stock. Once you choose a pack, you put it on each account's guide, tied to your SKUs. Customers build the order by voice in the VOS app, then review each line before sending.
